newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU COURT CONDEMNS BELGIAN RULES ON FOREIGN WORKERS.
newsitem.headline: EU COURT CONDEMNS BELGIAN RULES ON FOREIGN WORKERS.

text.p: Belgium cannot order citizens from other European Union countries to leave the country if they have not found jobs within three months, the European Court of Justice ruled on Thursday.
That violates the fundamental right of EU citizens to seek work across the Union, the court said.

It said countries may require unsuccessful jobhunters to leave after a "reasonable period", but not before they are given a chance to prove they are continuing to seek work and have a genuine chance of finding it.
The court also condemned two other Belgian laws involving workers from other EU countries.

One requires those planning to stay for at least one year to obtain and pay for two three-month registration certificates -- instead of a residence permit -- during their first six months in the country.
Another requires those expecting to stay for no more than three months to obtain and pay for a residence document.
The court upheld the European Commission, which argued that the rules represented financial and administrative obstacles to the free movement of workers.
